cases.label: drop
cases.note: Published RFC text: the nonexistent instance is ignored and not counted, so COUNT=4 reaches 2026-03-10.

cases.label: pre-gap-offset
cases.note: Erratum 4271 routed through §3.3.5: 02:30 EST = 07:30Z, which is 03:30 EDT in wall-clock terms.

expectation.note: python-dateutil emits 2026-03-08T02:30:00-04:00, a datetime for which dateutil.tz.datetime_exists() returns False: it neither drops the instance nor resolves it via the pre-gap offset.

normative_evidence.quote: Recurrence instances falling on invalid dates and times are ignored and not counted
invalid dates keep MUST-ignore; nonexistent local times are 'handled as specified in Section 3.3.5'
If the local time described does not occur ... the DATE-TIME value is interpreted using the UTC offset before the gap.

rationale: Three positions on nonexistent local times — published RFC, Verified erratum, and the most-used reference implementation — and none is what a user would predict. This is the vector that most directly falsifies 'RFC 5545 compliant' as a claim.
title: Daily 02:30 across the US spring-forward gap
